prompt.context: Our client is the president of Zippy Snowmobiles. It makes snowmobiles for recreational users only. Zippy has faced falling sales over the past 7 years, of 7% per year, or about 40% over that period. Zippy's president has hired McKinsey to investigate and reverse this trend.
prompt.question: What areas would you like to explore in order to investigate and reverse Zippy's falling revenues?

clarifying_info.q: What is the overall market trend during the same period?
clarifying_info.a: Refer candidate to Exhibit 1 for market data.

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected market change from 2008 to 2009?
clarifying_info.a: The overall market is expected to decline 8% from 2008 to 2009.

clarifying_info.q: What is the retail price of each snowmobile?
clarifying_info.a: The retail price of each snowmobile is $50,000.

clarifying_info.q: What is the variable cost of producing each snowmobile?
clarifying_info.a: The variable cost of producing each snowmobile is $20,000.

exhibits.title: Snowmobile Revenues (USD) from 2001–2008 in North America
exhibits.shows: A multi-year revenue bar chart (2001–2008) for Zippy and its competitors (Northpoint, Gemco, Sierra) in the North American snowmobile market.
exhibits.data: Total market 2002 ≈ $190M; Zippy 2002 ≈ $75M; Total market 2008 ≈ $120M; Northpoint absent after ~2004; Gemco revenue increases after Northpoint disappears; Sierra's share grows despite overall decline.

exhibits.title: Number of Zippy Snowmobiles Sold in One Year
exhibits.shows: A bar or table showing number of Zippy snowmobiles sold annually, with 2009 projection showing an incremental 100 units from the proposed gas-card promotion.
exhibits.data: Current baseline sales shown; incremental units from promotion = 100; total cards issued = 1,100.

framework: Market: Assess overall market size and growth trend, competitive landscape, and key success criteria
Revenue: Analyze pricing, sales volumes, product mix, and seasonal balance
Costs: Ensure proposed solutions do not overextend costs (e.g., diseconomies of scale) and maintain profitability
Risks: Stress-test any improvement proposal by identifying potential risks and barriers

questions.prompt: Examine Exhibit 1 and assess the market situation.
questions.guidance: Strong answers should note: (1) The overall market has shrunk ~40% over the 7-year period, so Zippy's decline mirrors an industry-wide problem, not just a company-specific issue. (2) Northpoint has disappeared — possibly acquired by Gemco, whose revenue spiked afterward; Northpoint's demise holds cautionary lessons. (3) Sierra has actually grown market share in a declining market — its strategies may offer best-practice clues.

questions.prompt: What revenue growth strategies could Zippy pursue?
questions.guidance: Suggested strategies include: M&A with other players (e.g., acquire Sierra or study Gemco); organic growth using the Ansoff Matrix (market penetration, product development, market development, diversification); revenue maximization tactics (bundling, tying, loss-leader); product line extension for seasonal balance (complementary summer products); geographic expansion (overseas or new regions); segmentation/blue-ocean strategies targeting underserved niches such as children or physically challenged users.

questions.prompt: The CEO wants to know what increase in market share is needed in 2009 compared to 2008, in order to maintain the same revenue dollars as in 2002. (The overall market is expected to decline 8% from 2008 to 2009 — share this only if asked.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should anchor on Zippy's 2002 revenue as the target, calculate 2009 total market size, and solve for required share. A strong answer clearly states the baseline share and required share, then computes the delta both in percentage points and as a percent of the baseline.

math.setup: Target revenue = Zippy 2002 revenue = $75M. 2009 total market = 2008 total market × (1 - 8%). Zippy 2002 market share = Zippy 2002 revenue / 2002 total market. Required 2009 share = Target revenue / 2009 total market.
steps: Increase in market share = 70% - 40% = 30 percentage points (or ~75% increase relative to the 40% base)
math.answer: Zippy needs to grow its market share from ~40% to ~70%, an increase of ~30 percentage points (or roughly 75% relative increase), to maintain 2002 revenue levels in 2009.

questions.prompt: The CMO proposes a gas-card promotion (Exhibit 2). Assess the incremental profits: every Zippy purchase includes a $200 gas card with a 30% redemption rate; the promotion is expected to generate 100 incremental unit sales; total cards issued = 1,100.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate incremental contribution margin from additional units, then subtract total cost of redeemed gas cards. Providing additional facts (retail price, variable cost) only when asked is good interview practice.

math.setup: Incremental profit = Additional units × (Price - Variable Cost) - (Redemption rate × Gas card value × Total cards issued)
math.answer: Incremental profit from the gas-card promotion ≈ $2.94M

brainstorming.prompt: What revenue growth strategies could Zippy pursue to reverse its declining sales?

categories.name: M&A
ideas: Study Gemco's post-Northpoint integration for lessons
Acquire or partner with international snowmobile brands

categories.name: Organic Growth (Ansoff Matrix)
ideas: Market penetration: increase share in existing North American market
Product development: add complementary summer products for seasonal balance
Market development: expand to new geographies (overseas, new regions)
Diversification: explore adjacent outdoor recreation products

categories.name: Revenue Optimization
ideas: Loss-leader pricing on entry models to build volume

categories.name: Customer Segmentation / Blue Ocean
ideas: Design adapted products for physically challenged users
Create premium/luxury segment for high-income enthusiasts

recommendation: Zippy's falling revenues mirror a decline of the industry as a whole, not a company-specific failure
Reversing the trend requires a combination of organic growth measures and strategic M&A
risks: M&A integration risk if acquiring Sierra or another player
Seasonal balance initiatives may require significant R&D investment
Market may continue to contract regardless of Zippy's moves
Gas-card and similar promotions add cost; margin must be monitored
next_steps: Pursue organic growth: extend product line for seasonal balance and explore new geographic markets
Evaluate gas-card promotion for full rollout given $2.94M incremental profit potential
Conduct due diligence and valuation on Sierra as an M&A target
Study Northpoint's demise for cautionary lessons before committing to any aggressive growth path
